data.reasoning: The only valid audit report (deepseek-v4-flash) correctly identified the PKGBUILD as a standard, safe build script that fetches a pinned source tarball from the official upstream GitHub repository. The 'inconclusive' result from qwen3-235b was due to a transient API error (HTTP 400), not a genuine security ambiguity. The advisory report also confirmed the package is safe.
data.disagreement_analysis: The disagreement was artificial, caused by a tool error (HTTP 400 BadRequestError) in the qwen3-235b model when attempting to audit the PKGBUILD and .SRCINFO files, rather than a substantive difference in security analysis.
coverage_issues: qwen3-235b-a22b-2507 failed to audit PKGBUILD and .SRCINFO due to LLM API HTTP 400 errors, resulting in a missing verdict signal.
learnings: The audit tool should distinguish between 'inconclusive due to tool/API failure' and 'inconclusive due to ambiguous code'. Transient API errors should trigger automatic retries or be flagged as tool failures rather than generating an 'inconclusive' security verdict that triggers costly escalation workflows.
